page: Amazon Web Services m9g.48xlarge is a general-purpose, ninth-generation instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features custom AWS Graviton processors based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 core architecture, running at a nominal frequency of 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 192 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapped directly to 192 vCPUs. Memory capacity stands at 768.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Cache layout consists of 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core, alongside 96 MB of shared L3 cache. There is no bundled local instance storage and no integrated GPU acceleration, while network infrastructure provides a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results show dominant multi-threaded execution and high memory throughput across intensive workloads. The instance achieves a top-tier multi-core score of 381,353.24 on stress-ng, supported by a 107,221.26 PassMark CPU score and 1,940.04 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput. Uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth benchmarks reach 729.22 GB/sec for reads and 327.62 GB/sec for writes, reflecting strong interconnect density. In transactional tests, the system handled 507.16 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 359.97 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core stress-ng performance falls into the middle 50% tier at 2,008.79, and LLM text generation throughput shows notable bottlenecks common to CPU-bound inference.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers cost-efficient compute and memory balance for scaled parallel jobs, minimizing idle infrastructure overhead in workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. AWS m9g.48xlarge is well suited for enterprise database clusters, distributed caching fleets, high-concurrency microservices, data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput static web workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores clocked at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is configured with 768.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 100 Gbps baseline networking, no bundled local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation reveals top-tier multi-core and memory subsystem performance, including 381,353.24 on stress-ng multi-core, 729.22 GB/sec uncached large-block read memory bandwidth, and 507.16 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Single-threaded compute shows average baseline throughput, and LLM generation remains limited due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. The architecture offers high resource efficiency for high-density horizontal workloads. AWS m9g.48xlarge is suited for scalable web services, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, distributed databases, batch ETL processing, and parallelized multi-threaded tasks.
